title: Application Estate Monitoring, Reporting & Supportability (Microsoft Graph & Power BI)
author_notes: pricing: T3 — Intune + Graph + Power BI, 3 technologies (multi-component reporting pipeline within the endpoint platform; matches the $2,495 Intune app-troubleshooting reference).

Scope boundary: this is the MONITORING/REPORTING/SUPPORTABILITY layer of application management (deployment health KPIs, SLO, Graph->storage->Power BI pipeline, 3-view dashboard, alerting, supportability model). It is NOT license/cost reporting (that is the separate LICRPT/SAM discipline) and NOT per-install troubleshooting (that is INTAPPDX). Boundary stated explicitly in 01-solution-overview.md 'What this solution is NOT'.

gov_variant: false — decision + reasoning: US Gov clouds DO use different endpoints (Graph graph.microsoft.us/dod-graph.microsoft.us, Connect-MgGraph -Environment USGov/USGovDoD, portals endpoint.microsoft.us/portal.azure.us, and a SEPARATE Power BI Government cloud app.powerbigov.us with parity gaps). However the METHOD is identical across clouds — only URLs and one script parameter change. This is handled inline: all five scripts take -Environment Global|USGov|USGovDoD and route Graph accordingly; Requirements R11 carries the full endpoint substitution table; Implementation Step 0 selects the cloud; Best Practices + Troubleshooting T8 cover the separate Power BI Gov workspace and parity caveats ('verify for GCC High'). A separate source-gov\ variant would duplicate near-identical content, so inline documentation is sufficient and preferred. Did NOT invent GCC High specifics; flagged uncertain parity as 'verify for GCC High'.

Adoption KPI honesty: Intune has no native per-app launch telemetry for Windows desktop apps; the solution instructs assembling adoption from M365/Defender/Endpoint-analytics/vendor signals and labeling confidence, rather than presenting an unsourced number.
